name: AL-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by 17 points and incumbent Gary Palmer is seeking re-election
Democratic challenger Maurice Mercer raised under $7,000 with no outside support
Prediction markets give Republicans roughly 97 percent
No polls or expert ratings; fundamentals carry the forecast
model.rationale: The forecast rests on the district's strong Republican lean combined with Palmer's incumbency and a roughly 175-to-1 fundraising advantage; markets price the race at about 97 percent Republican, and the challenger's negligible war chest signals a token campaign. Everything measurable points the same direction, so the expected margin sits slightly beyond the district's partisan lean.
model.watch: A major scandal or sudden influx of outside spending against Palmer could narrow the margin, though the seat is very unlikely to become competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 6th District, centered on suburban Birmingham, is firmly Republican territory with a partisan lean of roughly 17 points toward the GOP. Gary Palmer, the incumbent, is running for another term and has raised over $1.1 million. His Democratic challenger, Maurice Mercer, has raised under $7,000 and reported less than $2,000 on hand, with no outside groups active on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings track this contest, but prediction markets give Palmer roughly a 97 percent chance of winning. The combination of a heavily Republican electorate, an established incumbent, and a challenger without the resources to run a competitive campaign makes this one of the least competitive House races on the ballot. The realistic question is the size of Palmer's victory margin, not which party carries the seat.
